summary: builder-II (614 commits, 662 tracked files, single author, hosted at git@git.acbcontent.org:core-labs/builder-II.git on private Forgejo) has zero open-source table stakes today: no LICENSE, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, CHANGELOG.md, no issue/PR templates, no .forgejo/ or .gitea/ directory, and no git tags ever cut despite a v0 "release proof harness" and pyproject version 0.1.0. The only CI is a GitHub-idiom workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml) whose header literally documents GitHub.com branch protection and whose gitleaks-action step depends on GITHUB_TOKEN/GitHub APIs. The 481-line README is philosophy-first — the Install section starts at line 380 — and contains marketing claims ("rock-solid", "flawlessly supports") that contradict the repo's own "Not yet promoted" validation boundary. The docs/ directory is a 112-entry flat pile with no index; OPERATOR_QUICKSTART.md hardcodes the operator's personal machine paths. Pre-publication hygiene is nontrivial: 22 tracked files contain personal identifiers, all commits carry a personal iCloud email, and 172 remote branches plus a stash exist beyond main. The good news: .env was never committed, .env.example is clean, version strings are consistent, and the history filename scan shows no obvious credential-file additions — so a full-history secret scan is likely to pass, but must still be run across all refs before any gifting.

dependencies: Pre-publication history and PII hygiene pass

risks: Publishing without a LICENSE makes the gift legally void — recipients have no usage rights; this blocks everything else and is currently absent (no license file, no pyproject license field).

The 172 remote branches (including backup/main-before-reset-20260628-191623) and 1 stash have never been content-scanned; a HEAD-only or working-tree-only scan (which is all ci.yml lines 44-78 provides) is insufficient evidence of a clean history before publication.

Operator PII is woven through history and content: assetoverflow@icloud.com on all 614 commits, '<developer_name>' paths and '<developer_name>' in 22 tracked files — once pushed to a public host this is irreversible, and any history rewrite after tagging v0.1.0 would invalidate the tag.

README marketing claims ('rock-solid', 'flawlessly supports' Vertex/Groq/xAI at lines 192-202) contradict the repo's own 'Not yet promoted' boundary (lines 364-376); for the stated audience of skeptical senior engineers this undermines the project's core truth-first pitch and its own `builder-platform audit-docs` ethos.

CI green-status on Forgejo is unverified: gitleaks-action and the GITHUB_TOKEN secret may silently no-op or fail on Forgejo Actions, `ubuntu-latest` may not map to any registered runner, and `uv sync --all-groups` pulls mlx-lm/rapid-mlx on a Linux runner — the pipeline may never have actually run on the current host.

Hard Apple-Silicon M1 dependency (pyproject mlx-lm/rapid-mlx, README line 261 hardware target) sharply narrows the beta audience; non-Mac engineers cannot complete `uv sync`, and nothing in the README warns them before they clone.

Tracked agent-instruction files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .cursorrules) reference private infrastructure ('private Forgejo server', git.acbcontent.org conventions); shipping them unedited leaks internal hosting details and gives external contributors instructions that don't apply to them.
scripts/install-goose.sh falls back to curl-piping an unpinned remote script from a github.com release URL — a supply-chain exposure to flag in SECURITY.md or pin by checksum before public release.
